text.p: Doubletree Corp Chief Financial Officer William Perocchi said Tuesday the company was comfortable with analysts' earnings-per-share estimates of $1.50 for 1997.
"We continue to be comfortable with consensus estimates," he said.
Speaking at a Montgomery Securities Hospitality Conference, Chief Executive and President Richard Kelleher said the company expects to grow earnings per share by "at least 25 percent per year."
Kelleher said the company seeks to grow through improvement of existing business, addition of rooms, new strategic partnerships, increased support services and new acquisitions.
He said he sees significant revenue-per-available-room (revPARR) growth as the company converts Red Lion hotels to Doubletree hotels.
Red Lion Hotels was acquired by Doubletree in November 1996.
Kelleher said that 40 to 45 Red Lion properties were to be converted to the Doubletree brand, and that the conversion would result in one-time capital costs of $10 to $15 million.
He said the Renaissance Hotel Group N.V. proposed acquisition will double the size of Doubletree when completed. The deal was seen closing in the second quarter, he said.
Doubletree Corp is a hotel management company and the exclusive franchisor of Doubletree Hotels, Doubletree Guest Suites, and Club Hotels by Doubletree hotel brands.
